The *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 20.5) is a text of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka located within the *Paṭṭhāna* [SuttaCentral]. In the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), the *mahantaraduka* represents the "longer intermediate set of fourteen dyads," an established category of factors wherein numerous couplets analyze the mutual relationships between consciousness and mental states [Potter 1996]. Within the combinatorial system of the *Paṭṭhāna*, this section treats the conditional relations structuring these fourteen dyads [Potter 1996]. The secondary literature in the dossier does not study Patthana 20.5 directly, referring to the *mahantaraduka* primarily in the context of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* and *Dhātukathā* matrices [Potter 1996].

No curated parallels in other languages or traditions are listed by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or greater [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records widespread Pali-internal textual reuse typical of the *Paṭṭhāna*, consisting of 1,852 matching segments distributed across 209 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest text-reuse relationships are found with related sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, particularly *Mahantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.10; 125 matches, including §11.1_0–13.1 aligned with §60.1_0–62.1_1), *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 84 matches), and *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 20.8; 72 matches, including §1.1_0–3.1 aligned with §27.1_1–29.1) [DharmaNexus].
